paper.title: Regret Minimization in Bilateral Trade With Perturbed Markets

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated bilateral trade in perturbed markets, distributional benchmark OPT^D (one-bit feedback, global budget balance)
unmapped: Bilateral trade: learner posts seller price p_t and buyer price q_t in [0,1]; reward is gain from trade (b_t - s_t) I(s_t<=p_t, b_t>=q_t)
One-bit feedback: only whether the trade occurred is observed
Global budget balance: cumulative revenue sum_t (q_t-p_t) I(trade) must be >= 0 almost surely
Corruption C defined as sum_t ||L_t - P||_TV between per-round valuation distributions and an unperturbed distribution P
Unperturbed distribution P is sigma-smooth w.r.t. uniform measure
Benchmark: best distribution over price pairs budget-balanced in expectation over the horizon
settings.definition_quote: The environment is characterized by a probability distribution $\cP\in [0,1]^2$, representing the private valuations distribution in the unperturbed market. Moreover, there is a perturbation parameter $C$, which is defined as the cumulative total variation distance between the sequence of distributions $\{\cL_t\}_{t =1}^T$ chosen by the adversary and the unperturbed stationary distribution $\cP$: $C \coloneq \sum_{t=1}^T \lVert \cL_t - \mathcal{P} \rVert_{\textnormal{TV}}$.

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated bilateral trade (adversarial), fixed-price benchmark OPT^F (one-bit feedback, global budget balance)
unmapped: Bilateral trade: learner posts seller price p_t and buyer price q_t in [0,1]; reward is gain from trade
One-bit feedback: only whether the trade occurred is observed
Global budget balance: cumulative revenue must be >= 0 almost surely
Valuations drawn from time-varying distributions L_t chosen by an oblivious adversary; no smoothness required
Benchmark: best fixed price p (posted to both sides)
settings.definition_quote: These valuations are realizations of a joint time-dependent probability distribution $\mathcal{L}_t$ with support in $[0,1]^2$, chosen by an oblivious adversary. ... $\opt^{\,\textnormal{F}} := \max_{p \in [0, 1]} \sum_{t=1}^T \gft_t(p, p)$.

algorithms.name: No-Regret Algorithm (Algorithm 1: alternating Rev-Max and Primal-Dual with EXP3.IX-style primal)

conditions: unperturbed distribution P is sigma-smooth, sigma treated as a constant
algorithm is global budget balanced almost surely
tuning: grid size K = T^{1/4} (paper writes T^{-1/4})

source.label: theo: main
source.quote: There exists a GBB algorithm that, with probability $1-\cO(1/T)$, guarantees: \[ \sum_{t=1}^T \gft_t(p_t,q_t)\ge \max\{ \opt^{\,\textnormal{D}}- O(C\log(T)), \opt^{\,\textnormal{F}} \} - \tilde \cO(T^{3/4}) . \]

results.notes: Regret against best distribution over price pairs budget-balanced in expectation. Mixed notation: Õ(T^{3/4}) + O(C log T); recorded as O_tilde. C need not be known.

conditions: algorithm is global budget balanced almost surely
tuning: grid size K = T^{1/4} (paper writes T^{-1/4})
